page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Left margin holds four marginal notes (1.Reg. references and "David in regem ungitur", and a note "a monomachiam"). Running head at top. Page number at top left. Catchword at bottom right. Show-through or edge marks at bottom left, not transcribed.

main_text.p: mini ira compertum est, morte affici filiū jussit. Sed populi auxilio ab exitio vindicatus est. Ea tempestate Samuel a Domino monitus, regem adiit verbis Domini nuncians, uti géti Amalech, quæ olim Hebræos ex Aegypto venientes transitu prohibuerat, bellum inferret: addito interdicto, ne quid ex spoliis devictorū concupisceret. Ita in fines hostiū ductus exercitus, rex capt[?], gēs subacta. Saul victus prædæ magnitudine, præcepti divini immemor, capta servari & ferri jubet. Quo facto offensus Dominus, Samuelē alloquitur: pœnitere se, quod Saul regē constituerit.1.Reg.[?] Dictū sacerdos regi refert. Mox a Domino monitus, David regali unguēto per-[?]init, parvum etiamnum puerum, sub patre agentem, pastorem ovium, assuetū sæpius cithara canere: ob quod posteā a Saule assumptus, inter ministros regios habebatur.1.Reg.16. Qua tēpestate, Allophylis atq; Hebræis bello flagrātibus, cum ex adverso acies constitissent, Goliath quidā ex Allophylis, vir mirae magnitudinis & roboris, suorū ordines prætergressus, ferocibus verbis probra in hostes jaciēs, {a}singulare pugnā ciebat.monomachiam 1Reg.17. page.notes: Margin notes: the first note reads "1.Reg.f" with the last letter doubtful. "David in regem ungitur" is set over three lines in the margin and is written here as one note. The word "per-[?]init" is damaged at the line end: the reading "unctus" is likely but not legible, so it is marked [?]. "capt[?]" has a raised abbreviation mark that is not clear. The text "ptias" at the foot is the catchword and not part of the running text. Show-through marks at the bottom left ("ichia", "rcprwrqJ") are not transcribed. Long s is written as s; printed "f" in "jufsit", "eft", "fines" is read as long s.
